dek: Jack Clark takes the singularity to the IMF, the self-improver rewrites its own tooling, and emergent misalignment reaches the reward models that supervise the rest.
brief: Jack Clark took the singularity to the IMF: his Per Jacobsson lecture in Bangkok (the full text is Import AI #477) argues 2026 delivered the first convincing evidence of AI operating at the frontier of human science — Humanity's Last Exam from 8% to 67.7% on Claude Opus 5.5, FrontierMath from 2% to 94%, AI-designed drugs in trials. The self-improvement exhibit meanwhile got both sharper and more honest: Self-HPO alternately optimizes an agent's harness and policy (the policy proposes its own harness from its failures), while a companion paper finds cold-start evolution repairs failures but rarely transfers the lessons — a “repair-generalization gap.”

Anthropic moved on capital-governance weeks before its IPO: 5% of shares committed to a new Public Benefit Fund, with 2% more added for every 50% increase in company value. And the misalignment story climbed a layer up: emergent misalignment now extends to reward models themselves — narrow harmful fine-tuning in one domain generalizes to seven others at a five-point RewardBench cost.

top_stories.title: The singularity goes to the IMF
top_stories.summary: Import AI 477 is the full text of Jack Clark's Per Jacobsson lecture in Bangkok (given Oct 17): 2026 brought the first convincing evidence of AI operating at the frontier of human science, sometimes autonomously — HLE 8% (Jan 2025) to 67.7% (Claude Opus 5.5), FrontierMath 2% to 94%, AI insights on the Navier-Stokes Millennium problem, AI-designed drugs now in trials, GPT-6-Astra scoring 98% on unpublished theoretical-physics problems (TheoPhysEval) while finding subtle errors in the experts' own answers.
top_stories.why: the singularity narrative moves from labs and papers into mainstream economic policymaking — Clark's pitch: AI multiplies researchers, so economists should prepare with foresight and restraint to share the benefits.

top_stories.title: The self-improver rewrites its own tooling — and a sobering counterpoint
top_stories.summary: Self-HPO (arXiv 2610.22791): a recursive self-improvement loop that alternately optimizes an agent's harness and its policy, each round the policy proposing its own harness from its failures, beating harness-only and policy-only baselines on three coding benchmarks. The counterweight (2610.22984): in cold-start failure-only evolution, agents repair previously failed tasks but rarely transfer the lessons to unseen ones — a “repair-generalization gap” that tempers RSI optimism.
top_stories.why: the sharpest RSI loop yet arrives in the same batch as its own limiting result.

top_stories.title: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to a Public Benefit Fund
top_stories.summary: Announced Oct 18: a wholly-owned LLC (not a nonprofit), with 2% more shares added at the board's discretion for every 50% increase in company value above a baseline — roughly 20% of shares dedicated to public benefit once co-founder pledges and the employee equity-match are counted. The fund gives Anthropic flexibility beyond in-company work: large donations to nonprofits, direct distributions.
top_stories.why: capital-governance arrives weeks before the IPO marketing week — the pacing agenda gets a balance-sheet layer.

top_stories.title: Emergent misalignment reaches the supervisors
top_stories.summary: “Compression Precedes, Content Decides” (arXiv 2610.22805): narrow harmful fine-tuning of reward models in one domain (medical or financial) generalizes to seven held-out domains while losing only ~5 points on RewardBench 2 — and reward models prove more vulnerable to preference inversions than their base LMs.
top_stories.why: emergent misalignment is no longer just a behavior of the models — it's in the models that supervise them.

blogs.body: Anthropic — “Investing in the public benefit”: 5% of shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund (wholly-owned LLC, not a 501(c)(3)), plus 2% for every 50% increase in company value above a baseline; combined with co-founder pledges and the employee equity-match, roughly 20% of shares will be dedicated to public benefit. More details and a public benefit report coming in the next months.

Import AI 477 — “In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun”: the full text of Jack Clark's Per Jacobsson lecture in Bangkok — the singularity's evidence (HLE 8%→67.7%, FrontierMath 2%→94%, AI-designed drugs in trials, AI remotely operating lab equipment), the upside case for multiplying researchers, and a call for economists to prepare with foresight and restraint.

videos.title: Gemini 4 Argon Really Surprised Me”
videos.summary: Working from the model card and safety report: a sparse mixture-of-experts design with 1M-token combined input/output context; leads on Vals Index and DeepSWE v1.1, trails on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Opus 5.5.

videos.title: How DeepSeek Uses Less Memory”
videos.summary: DeepSeek's memory-efficiency techniques — the KV-cache and token-compression work behind recent DeepSeek releases, including V4.1-Flash — in mainstream circulation.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
papers.body: Zhepei Wei, Wenlin Yao, Baolin Peng et al. — A recursive self-improvement loop that alternately optimizes an agent's harness and policy, each round the policy proposing its own harness from its failures; beats harness-only and policy-only baselines on three coding benchmarks.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Agents Can Repair Failures but Struggle to Generalize from Them
papers.body: Weixiang Zhao, Yichen Zhang, Yanyan Zhao et al. — In cold-start failure-only evolution, agents repair previously failed tasks but rarely transfer the lessons to unseen ones — a “repair-generalization gap” that tempers RSI optimism.

papers.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.body: Lewen Yan, Yanxu Zhu, Jie Zhang, Jing Shao — A single prompt-customizable CoT monitor beats general LLMs as monitors by up to ~30 points, hitting state-of-the-art on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark across 15,971 reasoning trajectories.

papers.title: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
papers.body: Dhruv Puri, Nikhil Prakash — Narrow harmful fine-tuning of reward models in one domain generalizes to seven held-out domains while losing only ~5 points on RewardBench 2; emergent misalignment extends to the models that supervise LLMs.

papers.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
papers.body: Uriel Dolev, Idan Schwartz, Yoav Goldberg — CoT controllability is dramatically higher when constraints are placed as self-instructions inside the model's own reasoning rather than in the user prompt; prior “low controllability” findings may be artifacts of how constraints were specified.

papers.title: GatewayBench: Unified Capability and Security Evaluation Platform for MCP Gateways
papers.body: Yitian Zheng, Zhaorun Chen, Haoyu Li, Bo Li — The first unified benchmark for MCP gateways: 524 tasks across six domains plus 11,118 real-world tools from 251 MCP servers, comparing flattened vs. hierarchical gateway designs as the tool surface scales.

papers.title: MS-Eval: Benchmarking Sub-Agent Delegation and Orchestration in MCP-Intensive Working Scenarios
papers.body: Bowen Ding, Qixin Wang, Lexing Ruan et al. — Main-agent/sub-agent delegation benchmarking finds open-source models largely competitive, but delegation raises cost with only contingent payoff: it improves open models' performance and efficiency while leaving closed models costlier with degraded performance.

papers.title: Sep-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning
papers.body: Yinlong Xu, Jianjian Huang, Zhengdong Zhou et al. — Implicit latent-space reasoning anchored on separator tokens with attention-decay compression that adaptively ends the latent thinking phase by query complexity: 56.8% on GSM8k-Aug at just 5.4 tokens on average.

papers.title: Blitz: Accelerating the Diffusion Modules of AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2
papers.body: Vinay Saji Mathew, Soundar Kumara, Gretta Kellogg, William K. M. Lai — A few-step distillation framework cuts AlphaFold3/Boltz-2 diffusion from 200 denoising steps to 8 while retaining teacher-level structural accuracy; AF3-Blitz even exceeds its teacher on several metrics.

papers.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
papers.body: Yuxing Chen, Zhisheng Zhang, Cheng Tang et al. — An evolvable agent harness coupling 80+ scientific operations with conditional skill induction (candidate skills reviewed by an independent agent before admission); beats MolClaw-CC results by 10.8pp on MolBench affinity comparison and 55% on mean top-three active hits.

threads.name: Coordinated frontier pacing
threads.update: The RSI exhibit got both sharper and more honest: Self-HPO (2610.22791) alternately optimizes an agent's harness and policy, each round the policy proposing its own harness from its failures — the self-improver now rewrites its own tooling. The counterweight, (2610.22984), finds cold-start failure-only evolution repairs failed tasks but rarely transfers lessons to unseen ones — a “repair-generalization gap” keeping RSI optimism honest. Oversight: OwlSight (2610.23670) hits SOTA on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark — the audit primitive every pacing proposal needs. Governance: Anthropic's Public Benefit Fund (5% of shares, +2% per 50% value increase, ~20% total with co-founder pledges) puts capital-governance weeks ahead of the IPO marketing week. And Clark's IMF lecture (Import AI 477) moves the narrative into mainstream economics — HLE 8%→67.7%, FrontierMath 2%→94%, AI-designed drugs in trials — with the risk side promised “in coming issues.”

threads.name: Tiered bio-capability access
threads.update: Two new instruments: Blitz (2610.23703) distills AlphaFold3/Boltz-2 diffusion from 200 denoising steps to 8 at teacher-level accuracy (AF3-Blitz exceeds its teacher on several metrics) — protein-structure generation gets cheap. DrugHarness (2610.23791): an evolvable drug-discovery agent harness (80+ scientific operations, skill induction reviewed by an independent agent) beating MolClaw-CC by 10.8pp on MolBench affinity comparison.

threads.name: Lab supremacy race
threads.update: Two Minute Papers' “Gemini 4 Argon Really Surprised Me” (Oct 19) reads the model card and safety report: sparse MoE, 1M-token combined input/output context, leading Vals Index and DeepSWE v1.1 while trailing Terminal-Bench 4.0 against GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Opus 5.5 — benchmark-flavored evidence for the contested tier on the paper-explainer flank. Import AI 477's IMF-stage numbers: Claude Opus 5.5 at 67.7% on Humanity's Last Exam (from 8% in Jan 2025), FrontierMath 2%→94%, GPT-6-Astra at 98% on TheoPhysEval's unpublished physics problems.

threads.name: Agent misalignment goes public
threads.update: The oversight batch: OwlSight (2610.23670) — a prompt-customizable CoT monitor beating general LLMs as monitors by ~30 points, SOTA on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark (15,971 trajectories); “Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To” (2610.23257) — controllability dramatically higher via self-instructions than user prompts, suggesting prior low-controllability findings were specification artifacts; “Compression Precedes, Content Decides” (2610.22805) — emergent misalignment extends to reward models: narrow harmful fine-tuning in one domain generalizes to seven held-out domains at ~5 points of RewardBench 2 cost, and RMs prove more vulnerable to preference inversions than their base LMs.
